audit.whatIsWrong: The two-item row is printed as Darius in both layers, directly under text that says the opposite three separate times: whys[6] 'every duel only gets worse for Darius as the game goes long', spikes[3] 'Your peak', and late 'This is where you take over for good.' The packet levelChart and the mirror audit both give that row to Fiora. Rows 3 and 5 are printed as Darius too, while the packet says Skill and whys[3] says 'keeps the trades even' and whys[5] says 'genuinely even... whoever wins the Riposte read wins the trade'.
audit.why: The chart was telling a Fiora player she loses the scaling 1v1 against Darius on a 52.94% lane, on the exact row her own page calls her peak.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Darius 3 / Darius 3 / Skill 5 / Skill 5 / Skill 5 / Fiora 6 / Fiora 7 in both layers, with all seven phases[].why rewritten. Rows 5 and 6 follow the mirror audit, which states explicitly that first item and two-plus items belong to Fiora.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why said 'Ravenous Hydra is your spike — force fights the moment it completes' while phases[5].side said Darius, and no cooldown appeared anywhere in the full layer.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s — by a wide margin the longest cooldown in Darius's kit and the entire basis for 'bait the hook, then fight'. Decimate is 9s at rank 1, Crippling Strike 5s, Noxian Guillotine 120s at rank 1 against your 110s Grand Challenge. Without the 26s number, 'engage when the pull is down' gives the player nothing to count.
audit.corrected: 26s written into phases[2].why, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[1].d; Grand Challenge's 110s into phases[4].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two interactions that decide extended trades are absent from the whole page. Decimate HEALS Darius off champions hit by the blade, so the outer-edge trade the page warns about is not just more damage — it is his sustain. And Hemorrhage does not merely tick: at five stacks he enrages and gains massive Attack Damage, which is the actual reason to break off, not the bleed chip itself. The dontsFull bodies also do not match their titles.
audit.why: 'Trade into his outer Q' and 'Get pulled into 5 bleed' were both correct warnings with filler underneath them. Stating the heal and the enrage threshold turns them into rules.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[0].d now names the five-stack enrage; dontsFull[2].d names the blade-versus-handle heal; dontsFull[1].d contrasts the 9s Decimate against the 26s Apprehend so the player knows which cast to spend Riposte on.
sources: enemyKit Q text (heals based on enemy champions hit by the blade)
enemyKit P text (enrages and gains massive Attack Damage at max stacks)

audit.whatIsWrong: diff is 'HARD' while tone is the green #3ddc97, diffRating is 4/10 and report[14].t reads 'Favoured matchup'. Four fields, three verdicts.
audit.why: 52.94% over 988 Emerald+ games is a favoured lane. 'HARD' is the outlier against the other three.
audit.corrected: diff set to EVEN, which agrees with the green tone and the 4/10 rating without overstating the edge.

audit.why: packet.defects flags 'Grand Challenge's' in whys[4] as a probable wrong ability name. FALSE POSITIVE — it is the real name with a possessive apostrophe. No edit made. Separately I kept every Riposte instruction phrased as parrying the pull without asserting that Apprehend counts as an immobilizing effect for the stun upgrade: Riot's Riposte text gives the condition but does not define the category, and Apprehend is described only as a pull. The content layer already promises the STUN outright in early, mid, spikes[1] and wants.you[0]; I left those alone rather than restate or delete them. Same open question the mirror audit recorded.

notes: The headline fix is the two-item row: both layers printed Darius as the winner of the scaling 1v1 on the row the page's own prose calls Fiora's peak three separate times, and the packet and the mirror audit both say Fiora. Rows 5 and 6 follow the mirror explicitly ('First item and two-plus items belong to Fiora'); row 3 follows the packet and whys[3] rather than the mirror's coarser 'levels 1-5 stay Darius'. packet.defects flags 'Grand Challenge's' in whys[4] — false positive, it is the real name with a possessive. Every Riposte instruction I wrote stops at 'parry the pull' without promising the stun, because whether Apprehend qualifies as an immobilizing effect for that upgrade is not answerable from the kits; the content layer already promises it outright in four places and I left those untouched.
